title: Spectral Measures and Borel Functional Calculus

items.title: Projection valued measure
items.statement: On a measurable space (X,Σ), a PVM E takes values in orthogonal projections on a complex Hilbert space H, satisfies E(∅)=0, E(X)=I, E(B∩C)=E(B)E(C), and E(∪B_n)x=Σ E(B_n)x in norm for pairwise disjoint B_n. Regular on a locally compact space means each finite positive scalar measure E_x is regular. Inner products are linear in the first variable. Here orthogonal projection means a bounded operator P with P²=P=P*, with no finite-dimensional restriction.

items.title: Weak and strong additivity of orthogonal projections
items.statement: For orthogonal projection values multiplicative on intersections, weak countable additivity and strong countable additivity are equivalent.
items.proof_plan: For disjoint B_n, partial sums P_N are orthogonal projections below E(∪B_n); the squared norm of (E(∪B_n)-P_N)x equals its quadratic pairing with x, which tends to zero by weak additivity. Strong implies weak by Cauchy–Schwarz.

items.title: Scalar and complex measures from a pvm
items.statement: E_x(B)=〈E(B)x,x〉 is positive finite with mass ||x||²; E_{x,y}(B)=〈E(B)x,y〉 is a finite complex measure, linear in x, conjugate-linear in y. Its variation is at most ||x||||y||.
items.proof_plan: Polarize quadratic measures using E_{x,y}=1/4 Σ_{k=0}^3 i^k E_{x+i^k y}. For each finite disjoint partition use Cauchy–Schwarz twice to bound Σ|〈E(B_j)x,y〉| by ||x||||y||.

items.title: Simple pvm integral is representation independent
items.statement: The simple integral is independent of its disjoint presentation, satisfies 〈(∫s dE)x,y〉=∫s dE_{x,y}, and ||(∫s dE)x||²=∫|s|² dE_x.
items.proof_plan: Refine two partitions by all intersections; use orthogonality. Its norm is the maximum of |a_j| over nonzero projections, with zero for the zero operator.

items.title: Bounded borel pvm integral
items.statement: Every bounded measurable complex f has a unique integral Φ_E(f), obtained from uniform simple approximations. It satisfies ||Φ_E(f)||≤||f||∞, the scalar pairing identity and ||Φ_E(f)x||²=∫|f|² dE_x. The exact norm is the E-essential supremum.
items.proof_plan: Approximate the bounded complex range by finite grids, prove the operators are norm Cauchy and the limit independent; pass the simple identities to limits. For the reverse essential-norm inequality use a nonzero spectral projection on {|f|>c}.

items.title: Pvm integral is a star homomorphism
items.statement: Φ_E is a unital star homomorphism. If f_n→f pointwise E-almost everywhere and sup_n||f_n||∞<∞, then Φ_E(f_n)→Φ_E(f) strongly.
items.proof_plan: First multiply simple functions on a common partition; uniform approximation proves products and adjoints. Apply scalar dominated convergence to ∫|f_n-f|² dE_x.

items.title: Positive continuous calculus yields a regular pvm
items.statement: For compact K⊂C and a unital star representation π:C(K)→B(H), there is a unique regular PVM E with π(f)=∫f dE for every continuous f.
items.proof_plan: Represent each positive functional 〈π(f)x,x〉 by a positive regular measure. Polarization and uniqueness give sesquilinear measures. Positivity yields |μ_xy(B)|²≤μ_x(B)μ_y(B)≤||x||²||y||², so Hilbert Riesz defines E(B). Scalar uniqueness applied first to π(f) and a continuous multiplier g, then to Borel sets in each variable, proves E(B)E(C)=E(B∩C). Thus E(B) is a self-adjoint projection. Scalar additivity and the preceding lemma give SOT additivity. Do not assume projection-valuedness from positivity alone.

items.title: Spectral theorem for bounded normal operators pvm form
items.statement: Every bounded normal T on H has a unique regular PVM on σ(T) with T=∫z dE(z). Conversely such an integral is normal.
items.proof_plan: Apply the preceding construction to the continuous calculus. For uniqueness a competing PVM gives the same polynomials in z and conjugate z; complex Stone–Weierstrass and scalar measure uniqueness finish. No powers-of-T-only density assertion.

items.title: Support and uniqueness of the spectral measure
items.statement: The support of the spectral PVM of bounded normal T is σ(T); it and all pairings are uniquely determined by T.
items.proof_plan: A point outside support has a bounded reciprocal on the support and is a resolvent point; a disk on which E vanishes contradicts the faithful continuous calculus using a nonzero continuous test function. Treat H={0} separately.

items.title: Cyclic vector and cyclic normal operator
items.statement: A vector x is cyclic when the closure of {f(T)x:f∈C(σ(T))} is H. For normal T this means the unital star algebra generated by T and T*, not only nonnegative powers of T. The same construction defines H_x for an arbitrary vector.

items.title: Cyclic spectral representation
items.statement: For cyclic x, f↦f(T)x extends to a unitary L²(σ(T),E_x)→H intertwining M_z with T and Borel multipliers with the Borel calculus. For arbitrary x its range is H_x.
items.proof_plan: The norm-square identity gives isometry, the published Radon L² density theorem on compact σ(T) gives the source completion, and cyclicity gives the range. Multiplication on continuous functions extends.

items.title: Maximal orthogonal family of cyclic reducing subspaces
items.statement: Every bounded normal operator admits a family of mutually orthogonal cyclic reducing subspaces whose Hilbert sum is H. General existence uses AC/Zorn; in separable H a given dense sequence constructs a finite or countable such family.
items.proof_plan: H_x is invariant under T and T*, hence reducing. Order orthogonal cyclic families by inclusion; unions bound chains. A nonzero vector in the orthogonal complement would enlarge a maximal family. In the separable version project the next vector of a fixed dense sequence onto the remaining complement.

items.title: Multiplication operator form of the bounded normal spectral theorem
items.statement: A bounded normal operator on arbitrary H is unitarily equivalent to the coordinate multiplier on an orthogonal Hilbert sum ⊕_j L²(σ(T),μ_j).
items.proof_plan: Define the Hilbert sum by square-summable families (at most countably many nonzero coordinates for each vector); finite partial sums are isometric and dense. Extend the sum of the cyclic unitaries and check it intertwines on a dense subspace.

items.title: Spectral multiplicity function in the separable case
items.statement: For nonzero separable H choose normalized cyclic measures μ_j and μ=Σ 2^(-j)μ_j (renormalize in the finite case). Let F_j={dμ_j/dμ>0} and m(z)=Σ_j1_{F_j}(z), a Borel function with values 1,2,…,∞ μ-a.e. Use the coordinate model K_m={v∈L²(μ;ell²):v_k=0 where m<k}, k starting at 1. The measure class means equality of null Borel sets.

items.title: Spectral multiplicity is preserved by intertwiners
items.statement: A unitary intertwining the coordinate multipliers in two separable spectral models preserves their scalar measure class and their fiber dimensions almost everywhere.
items.proof_plan: Intertwining T and T* intertwines continuous functions and then spectral projections by scalar uniqueness. Null projections identify measure class; transport to a common finite measure by square roots of Radon–Nikodym densities. Each coordinate matrix entry of the intertwiner commutes with all indicators, so it is multiplication by its value on 1 (boundedness follows by testing indicators). On one common conull set, countably many rational finite-vector tests give an isometry of each fiber, and the inverse matrix gives onto; dimensions agree. This fills the uniqueness argument abbreviated in the source.

items.title: Unitary equivalence classified by measure class and multiplicity
items.statement: Two bounded normal operators on nonzero separable complex Hilbert spaces are unitarily equivalent iff their scalar spectral measure classes on C coincide and multiplicity functions coincide almost everywhere for that class. No change of spectral coordinate is allowed. The zero space is a separate trivial class.
items.proof_plan: Existence of the model: multiply the jth cyclic coordinate by sqrt(dμ_j/dμ), then enumerate active coordinates in increasing j; measurability is explicit. Sufficiency uses Radon–Nikodym square-root transport. Necessity is the preceding intertwiner lemma. Inline ordered cyclic model: in the separable multiplicity representation, use the nested measurable sets {m≥j} and their scalar coordinate spaces L²({m≥j},μ). Their constant unit-coordinate vectors are cyclic; the measures μ restricted to these sets decrease in absolute-continuity order. A positive square-summable weighted sum of these cyclic vectors has scalar measure equivalent to μ, hence is a maximal spectral vector. Normalize nonzero cyclic measures; handle H=0 separately.

items.title: Stone resolvent formula for spectral projections
items.statement: For bounded self-adjoint T and real a<b, (2πi)^(-1)∫_a^b[(T-(t+iε))^(-1)-(T-(t-iε))^(-1)]dt tends strongly as ε↓0 to E((a,b))+(E({a})+E({b}))/2.
items.proof_plan: For fixed ε the integrand is operator-norm continuous; interchange the finite-interval Bochner integral and scalar pairings. Its scalar kernel is [arctan((b-λ)/ε)-arctan((a-λ)/ε)]/π, lies in [0,1], and tends to the displayed half-atom indicator. Apply bounded spectral convergence. The weighted bounded-continuous version follows from the same Poisson-kernel approximation, with tails controlled before the spectral limit.

items.title: Unbounded linear operator domain and graph
items.statement: An operator T:D(T)⊂H→H is linear with a specified linear domain. Its graph is {(x,Tx):x∈D(T)}⊂H⊕H. T⊂S means inclusion of graphs; equality requires equal domains and equal values.

items.statement: T is closable iff x_n→0 and Tx_n→y imply y=0. Its graph closure then is the graph of its least closed extension, denoted closure(T).

items.statement: A densely defined T is symmetric if T⊂T*, self-adjoint if T=T*, and essentially self-adjoint if its closure is self-adjoint. Symmetric operators are closable.

items.title: Symmetric need not be self adjoint
items.statement: On L²(0,1), let Tf=−if′ on AC[0,1] functions with f′∈L² and f(0)=f(1)=0. T is densely defined, closed and symmetric, while D(T*)={g∈AC[0,1]:g′∈L²}, T*g=−ig′. Thus T≠T*.

items.title: Resolvent and spectrum of a closed unbounded operator
items.statement: For closed T, z∈ρ(T) iff T-z:D(T)→H is bijective with bounded everywhere-defined inverse R_T(z)=(T-z)^(-1). Its spectrum is C\ρ(T).
items.proof_plan: The closed graph theorem supplies boundedness of the inverse when bijective; graph norm makes D(T) Banach. Include openness by Neumann series and R(z)-R(w)=(z-w)R(z)R(w) inline. Inline interval warnings: the maximal −i d/dx on AC[0,1] with derivative in L² has eigenvector e^(izx) for every complex z, hence full complex spectrum. The same expression with sole condition f(0)=0 has empty spectrum: (T-z)^(-1)g(x)=i∫_0^x e^(iz(x-s))g(s)ds, a bounded Volterra map into its domain. The AC primitive and graph estimates prove density and closedness.

items.title: Unbounded pvm integral is well defined and closed
items.statement: f(E) is densely defined and closed. Bounded truncations, or bounded pointwise approximants dominated by C|f| on D(f(E)), give the same action. f(E)*=conjugate(f)(E); real f gives a self-adjoint operator.

items.proof_plan: Dominated convergence gives strong continuity; the essential supremum of |e^(itx)−1| is 2. Its generator is the unbounded position operator. Inline characterization: a unitary group is norm-continuous iff its self-adjoint generator is bounded. Bounded generators give norm continuity by the exponential series; conversely, for unbounded spectral support choose |λ_n|→∞ in that support and t_n=π/λ_n. Functional calculus yields ||e^(it_n A)-I||=2, contradicting norm continuity.

items.title: Self adjoint extensions and deficiency indices
items.statement: The extension theorem is proved on the A page. Equal deficiency dimensions give existence; unequal dimensions exclude extensions in the same H. A supplied unitary gives the exact domain and action without any further choice.
